regional.syndrome: Sudden high fever with severe, often symmetrical polyarthralgia and rash; the name means 'that which bends up'. Arthritis persists for months to years in 30–40%. Neonatal infection from intrapartum transmission and neurological disease in older adults can be severe; deaths occur mainly via decompensation of comorbidity.
regional.headline: Alphavirus of the Semliki Forest complex causing explosive epidemics of febrile polyarthritis.
regional.prevention: Vector control; the virus-like particle vaccine Vimkunya is licensed from 12 years of age. The live-attenuated IXCHIQ was licensed first, but its US licence was suspended in August 2025 and the application withdrawn in January 2026 after vaccine-strain encephalitis and other serious adverse events.
regional.geography: Africa, Asia, Indian Ocean, Americas since 2013, with autochthonous outbreaks in southern Europe.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Fever and headache progressing to encephalitis with brainstem signs, segmental myoclonus and seizures; acute respiratory distress is prominent in the Bangladesh/India lineage. Relapsing and late-onset encephalitis occurs months to years after recovery.
regional.headline: Bat-borne paramyxovirus with case fatality of 40–75% and documented person-to-person transmission; a WHO priority pathogen requiring BSL-4 handling.
regional.prevention: Avoid raw date palm sap, cover sap collection pots, strict PPE and isolation for cases, pig-farm biosecurity. Vaccines are in clinical trials.
regional.geography: Malaysia, Singapore, Bangladesh, India (Kerala, West Bengal), Philippines.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Dengue fever: high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia/arthralgia ('breakbone fever'), rash. A minority progress at defervescence to dengue with warning signs or severe dengue — plasma leakage, shock, haemorrhage and organ impairment. Secondary infection with a different serotype raises severe-disease risk through antibody-dependent enhancement.
regional.headline: The most important arboviral infection of humans worldwide, with an estimated 100–400 million infections annually.
regional.prevention: Vector control, Wolbachia-based mosquito replacement, and the live-attenuated vaccines CYD-TDV (serostatus-restricted) and TAK-003.
regional.geography: Tropics and subtropics worldwide; expanding with vector range.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Fewer than 1% of infections become clinical, but encephalitis carries ~20–30% mortality and leaves neurological or psychiatric sequelae in a third to a half of survivors; parkinsonian and acute flaccid paralysis presentations are characteristic.
regional.headline: The leading cause of vaccine-preventable viral encephalitis in Asia.
regional.prevention: Highly effective inactivated and live-attenuated vaccines (e.g. IXIARO, SA 14-14-2) in routine childhood programmes; pig husbandry siting; vector control.
regional.geography: South, Southeast and East Asia, Papua New Guinea, northern Australia.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: No defined human syndrome; serological cross-reactivity within the clade complicates attribution.
regional.headline: Prototype of the Manzanilla clade — the sublineage that also contains Cat Que/Oya virus. Mainly detected in mosquitoes, pigs and birds.
regional.geography: Trinidad, South America, Southeast Asia (clade members).
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: Rotavirus H. Detected in human stool in Asia; also porcine. Clinical role unresolved.
regional.geography: Rotavirus H. Detected in human stool in Asia; also porcine. Clinical role unresolved.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.
